stories.headline: Anthropic Ships Claude Opus 4.7 With 87.6% SWE-bench Verified, New xhigh Effort Level

key_facts.fact: SWE-bench Verified jumps from 80.8% (Opus 4.6) to 87.6%, and SWE-bench Pro from 53.4% to 64.3%, putting Opus 4.7 ahead of GPT-5.4 (57.7%) and Gemini 3.1 Pro (54.2%) on multi-language coding tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: SWE-bench Verified jumps from 80.8% to 87.6%, a nearly 7-point gain that puts Opus 4.7 ahead of Gemini 3.1 Pro (80.6%). On SWE-bench Pro, the harder multi-language variant, Opus 4.7 goes from 53.4% to 64.3%, leapfrogging both GPT-5.4 (57.7%) and Gemini (54.2%).

key_facts.fact: Opus 4.7 introduces a new 'xhigh' effort level between high and max, now the default in Claude Code for all plans, plus 3x vision resolution upgrade to 3.75 megapixels (2,576px long edge).
key_facts.excerpt: Opus 4.7 handles images up to 2,576 pixels on the long edge — about 3.75 megapixels, roughly 3× the resolution ceiling of previous Claude models.

key_facts.fact: Tool use leads all models on MCP-Atlas at 77.3%, and computer use (OSWorld-Verified) climbs from 72.7% to 78.0%, ahead of GPT-5.4 (75.0%).
key_facts.excerpt: Opus 4.7 leads MCP-Atlas at 77.3%, ahead of Opus 4.6 (75.8%), GPT-5.4 (68.1%), and Gemini 3.1 Pro (73.9%).

key_facts.fact: Pricing unchanged at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens. Available via Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry.
key_facts.excerpt: Pricing stays the same as Opus 4.6: $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic explicitly states Opus 4.7 is 'less broadly capable' than Claude Mythos Preview, which leads on most benchmarks including 93.9% on SWE-bench Verified.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Mythos Preview | 93.9% ... Opus 4.7 is available now ... Anthropic is explicit that Claude Mythos Preview remains more broadly capable.

key_facts.fact: Cursor reported a jump from 58% to 70% on CursorBench, and Rakuten reported 3x more production task resolutions than on Opus 4.6.
key_facts.excerpt: Cursor reported a jump from 58% to 70% on CursorBench... Rakuten ran it through their fork of SWE-Bench and got 3× more production task resolutions than on 4.6.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches GPT-Rosalind, a Purpose-Built Model for Drug Discovery and Life Sciences

key_facts.fact: GPT-Rosalind is a frontier reasoning model optimized for biology, drug discovery, and translational medicine, available as a research preview in ChatGPT, Codex, and the API for qualified enterprise customers.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're introducing GPT‑Rosalind, our frontier reasoning model built to support research across biology, drug discovery, and translational medicine.

key_facts.fact: Launch partners include Amgen, Moderna, the Allen Institute, and Thermo Fisher Scientific. A free Life Sciences plugin for Codex connects to over 50 scientific tools and databases.
key_facts.excerpt: We are working with customers like Amgen, Moderna, the Allen Institute, Thermo Fisher Scientific, and others... We're also introducing a freely accessible Life Sciences research plugin for Codex, helping scientists connect models to over 50 scientific tools and data sources.

key_facts.fact: The model tops BixBench (real bioinformatics) among models with published scores, and exceeds GPT-5.4 on 6 of 11 LABBench2 tasks. On RNA sequence prediction it reaches the 95th percentile of human experts.
key_facts.excerpt: BixBench (reële bio-informatica): Beste prestatie onder de modellen met gepubliceerde scores. LABBench2: Overschrijdt GPT-5.4 op 6 taken van de 11. RNA-sequentievoorspelling (Dyno Therapeutics): Top 95e percentiel van menselijke experts.

key_facts.fact: Only one in 10 drugs entering clinical trials ultimately gets approved, and no fully AI-discovered drug has made it through phase 3 trials yet.
key_facts.excerpt: Only one in 10 drugs entering clinical trials ultimately gets approved... No fully AI-discovered or AI-designed drug has made it through phase 3 trials.

key_facts.fact: The model is named after Rosalind Franklin. It was built on top of OpenAI's newest internal models and is deployed through a trusted-access program with enterprise-grade security controls.
key_facts.excerpt: The GPT-Rosalind, named after 20th-century British scientist Rosalind Franklin, is designed to support research across biochemistry, drug discovery and translational medicine.

stories.headline: OpenAI Codex Desktop Gains Mac Computer Control, In-App Browser, and 90+ New Plugins

key_facts.fact: Codex desktop app now includes a 'computer use' feature that lets agents operate Mac apps in the background — viewing the screen, clicking, and typing with their own cursor — while users continue working uninterrupted.
key_facts.excerpt: Codex can use desktop apps on your Mac in the background while you actively use your machine without interruption. 'Multiple agents can work in parallel, without interfering with your own work in other apps.'

key_facts.fact: A built-in browser based on OpenAI's Atlas browser lets users comment directly on web page elements to give Codex precise modification instructions, initially for local web apps.
key_facts.excerpt: Codex is bringing Atlas technology into the stack with its own in-app browser... lets you 'comment directly on pages to provide precise instructions to the agent.'

key_facts.fact: Image generation via gpt-image-1.5 is now integrated directly into Codex workflows. Over 90 new plugins ship with the update, combining skills, app integrations, and MCP servers.
key_facts.excerpt: Image generation, powered by OpenAI's gpt-image-1.5 model, is now directly woven into Codex's workflow... With over 100 new plugins and a growing user base of 3 million weekly users.

key_facts.fact: Automation now supports scheduling future work and resuming multi-day tasks automatically. A memory feature remembers user preferences and past corrections across sessions.
key_facts.excerpt: Codex can now reuse existing conversation threads, preserving context to schedule future work and automatically resume long-term tasks that span days or weeks.

key_facts.fact: The app has 3 million weekly users. Computer Use feature is macOS-only and not yet available in the EU. The update also adds Intel Mac support for the first time.
key_facts.excerpt: With over 100 new plugins and a growing user base of 3 million weekly users... The Computer Use feature is currently available only on macOS and is not yet available in the EU.

stories.headline: Alibaba Releases Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, an Open-Weight MoE Model That Rivals Dense Models 10x Its Active Size

key_facts.fact: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is a sparse MoE model with 35B total parameters but only 3B active per token (256 experts, 8+1 activated per layer), reducing compute by ~90% versus dense architecture.
key_facts.excerpt: The model contains 256 expert sub-networks but only activates 8 experts plus 1 shared expert per layer—just 9 total. This results in 3 billion active parameters despite a 35 billion parameter model, reducing compute by ~90%.

key_facts.fact: Scores 73.4% on SWE-bench Verified, beating Google's Gemma4-31B by 21.4 points. On Terminal-Bench 2.0, it scores 51.5% vs Gemma4-31B's 42.9%.
key_facts.excerpt: On SWE-bench Verified, it scores 73.4%, beating Google's Gemma4-31B by 21.4 points... On Terminal-Bench 2.0, which tests shell command generation, Qwen3.6 scores 51.5% versus Gemma4-31B's 42.9%.

key_facts.fact: Released under Apache 2.0 license with no usage restrictions. A quantized 21GB version runs on consumer hardware like an RTX 4090 or M5 MacBook.
key_facts.excerpt: Released under Apache 2.0 license... A quantized 21GB version runs on an $800 RTX 4090 or M5 MacBook.

key_facts.fact: Natively multimodal, supporting text, image, and video inputs. Processes hour-long videos with up to 224K video tokens and scored 83.7% on VideoMMU, highest in its class.
key_facts.excerpt: Qwen3.6 is natively multimodal, supporting text, image, and video inputs simultaneously. It can process hour-long videos with up to 224K video tokens and scored 83.7% on VideoMMU.

key_facts.fact: Introduces a 'thinking preservation' option to retain reasoning context from historical messages, improving multi-turn agentic workflows.
key_facts.excerpt: Thinking Preservation: we've introduced a new option to retain reasoning context from historical messages.

stories.headline: Physical Intelligence's π0.7 Shows First Signs of Compositional Generalization in Robotics

key_facts.fact: π0.7 is a steerable generalist robotic foundation model that exhibits compositional generalization — recombining skills from training data to solve tasks it was never explicitly trained on.
key_facts.excerpt: π0.7 exhibiting the first signs of compositional generalization, recombining skills from various tasks to solve new problems, like using new kitchen appliances and even enabling a new robot to fold laundry for which there is no laundry folding data.

key_facts.fact: In an air fryer experiment, with effectively only 2 pieces of training data related to the device, π0.7 successfully cooked sweet potatoes when given step-by-step language instructions — success rate rose from 5% to 95% after 30 minutes of prompt refinement.
key_facts.excerpt: Researchers said there were effectively only 2 pieces of training data directly related to the device. Even so, pi 0.7 attempted to cook sweet potatoes without additional training... success rate in the initial air fryer experiment stayed at about 5 percent, but rose to 95 percent after improving the way the task was explained.

key_facts.fact: The model provides zero-shot cross-embodiment transfer — enabling a robot to fold laundry without any laundry-folding data — and matches the performance of specialized RL-finetuned models on dexterous tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: π0.7 can follow diverse language instructions in unseen environments... provide zero-shot cross-embodiment generalization, for example enabling a robot to fold laundry without seeing the task before, and perform challenging tasks... at a level of performance that matches much more specialized RL-finetuned models.

key_facts.fact: Co-founder Sergey Levine compared the emergent capabilities to early LLM scaling, saying when robots move from performing only trained tasks to combining them in new ways, 'the magnitude of performance improvement grows.'
key_facts.excerpt: Co-founder Sergey Levine said, 'If you move beyond a stage where you perform only precisely trained tasks and move to a stage where you combine them in new ways, the magnitude of performance improvement grows.' He added, 'This is similar to scaling characteristics seen in language and vision models.'

key_facts.fact: Physical Intelligence has raised more than $1 billion to date and was recently valued at $5 billion. The researchers define π0.7 as an early signal still at research stage.
key_facts.excerpt: Physical Intelligence has raised more than $1 billion so far and was recently valued at $5... researchers defined pi 0.7 as an early signal of generalisation and an initial demonstration of new capabilities, and made clear it remains at a research stage.

stories.headline: OpenAI Doubles Cerebras Chip Commitment to $20B+, Gets Equity Stake Ahead of IPO

key_facts.fact: OpenAI agreed to pay Cerebras more than $20 billion over three years for servers powered by its chips, doubling the $10 billion deal struck in January for 750 MW of computing capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI has agreed to pay chip startup Cerebras more than $20 billion over the next three years... In January, the company agreed to buy up to 750 megawatts of computing capacity from Cerebras over three years in a deal valued at more than $10 billion.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI receives warrants for a minority stake in Cerebras that could grow to up to 10% if total spending reaches $30 billion over three years.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI will receive warrants for a minority stake in Cerebras, with its ownership potentially increasing as its spending rises... total spending over the next three years could reach $30 billion, which may translate into warrants representing up to a 10 per cent stake.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI also agreed to provide Cerebras about $1 billion to help fund data center development that would run OpenAI's AI products.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI has also agreed to provide Cerebras about $1 billion to help fund the development of data centers that would run its AI products.

key_facts.fact: Cerebras plans to disclose parts of the OpenAI arrangement as soon as Friday, as it targets an IPO raising $3 billion at a ~$35 billion valuation, up from $23.1 billion previously.
key_facts.excerpt: Cerebras could disclose parts of its previously undisclosed arrangement with OpenAI as soon as Friday... also plans to raise $3 billion in an offering next month at a valuation of circa $35 billion.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is an early investor in Cerebras. The deal highlights the growing appetite for computing power for inference workloads.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is an early investor in Cerebras... The deal highlights the industry's growing appetite for computing power to run inference.

stories.headline: Factory Raises $150M Series C at $1.5B Valuation for Model-Agnostic AI Coding Agents

key_facts.fact: Factory raised $150 million in Series C funding at a $1.5 billion valuation, led by Khosla Ventures with participation from Sequoia Capital, Insight Partners, and Blackstone.
key_facts.excerpt: Factory, a startup developing AI agents for enterprise engineering teams, announced it had raised $150 million at a $1.5 billion valuation. The round was led by Khosla Ventures, with participation from Sequoia Capital, Insight Partners, and Blackstone.

key_facts.fact: Factory's key differentiator is switching between different foundation models (Anthropic's Claude, DeepSeek, etc.) depending on task complexity. Its Droid product is used daily by hundreds of thousands of developers.
key_facts.excerpt: Factory founder Matan Grinberg told the Wall Street Journal that the company's key differentiator is its ability to switch between different foundation models, such as Anthropic's Claude or Chinese AI startup DeepSeek.

key_facts.fact: Enterprise customers include Morgan Stanley, Ernst & Young, Palo Alto Networks, NVIDIA, and Adobe. Revenue has doubled month-over-month for six consecutive months.
key_facts.excerpt: Droid is now used daily by hundreds of thousands of developers at enterprise clients such as NVIDIA, Adobe, Palo Alto Networks, EY, and Adyen. Over the past six months, the company has achieved month-over-month revenue doubling.

key_facts.fact: Use cases extend beyond code completion to include COBOL migration, legacy technical debt cleanup, and end-to-end automation from ticket to PR. New 'Missions' system supports long-duration multi-agent collaboration.
key_facts.excerpt: expanding its use cases beyond simple code completion to include COBOL migration, legacy technical debt cleanup, and end-to-end automation workflows from ticket to PR... Recent product advancements include the 'Missions' system, which supports long-duration, multi-step, multi-agent collaboration.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2023 by Matan Grinberg, a UC Berkeley PhD dropout who cold-emailed Sequoia's Shaun Maguire. Engineering team grew from 17 to 27 while valuation grew 10x.
key_facts.excerpt: The startup was founded in 2023 after Grinberg, then a PhD student at UC Berkeley, cold-emailed Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire.
